group.passage: Nearsightedness, or myopia, usually develops when the eyeball grows too long from front to back. Light then comes into focus in front of the retina instead of on it, so faraway objects look blurry. The condition often appears between the ages of 6 and 14 and can keep getting worse until a person's early twenties. In Taiwan, it became so common that by 2011, half of all primary school students had weak eyesight when tested without glasses. Studies have found that children who spend more time outdoors are less likely to become nearsighted, though experts are still not sure why. A study in southern Taiwan put this to the test. At one primary school, children were encouraged to go outside during class breaks, while a nearby school made no changes. After one year, 8.41 percent of the children at the first school had newly developed myopia, compared with 17.65 percent at the second. On a much larger scale, a national program called Tian-Tian 120 began in September 2010. It urged schools to give students 120 minutes outdoors every day. Between 2001 and 2011, the share of primary school students with weak eyesight had climbed steadily, from 34.8 percent to 50.0 percent. Then the trend turned around, and the figure fell every year from 49.4 percent in 2012 to 46.1 percent in 2015. The chart shows the picture in Taipei for more recent school years. It also reveals how much worse the problem becomes as children grow older: in every year shown, the rate for junior high students was far higher than the rate for elementary school students. The chart cannot explain why the numbers rose or fell in a particular year, and it does not prove that outdoor time alone caused any change. Still, together with the research, it suggests that protecting young eyes is not a one-time effort but a habit that has to be kept up year after year, both at school and at home.

translation_zh.text:
戶外活動與學童視力

近視通常是因為眼球從前到後長得太長而產生的。光線於是在視網膜前方就聚焦，而不是落在視網膜上，所以遠處的東西看起來模糊。這種狀況常在 6 到 14 歲之間出現，而且可能一直惡化到二十歲出頭。在台灣，近視變得非常普遍，到了 2011 年，全國有一半的小學生在不戴眼鏡受檢時視力不良。

研究發現，在戶外待得比較久的孩子比較不容易近視，雖然專家仍不確定原因。台灣南部的一項研究就把這一點拿來檢驗。一所小學鼓勵孩子在下課時間到戶外活動，附近另一所學校則維持不變。一年後，第一所學校有 8.41% 的孩子新出現近視，第二所學校則是 17.65%。

在更大的規模上，一項名為「天天戶外 120」的全國性計畫在 2010 年 9 月開始，鼓勵學校每天讓學生到戶外活動 120 分鐘。從 2001 年到 2011 年，小學生視力不良的比例一路攀升，從 34.8% 升到 50.0%。之後趨勢反轉，這個比例逐年下降，從 2012 年的 49.4% 降到 2015 年的 46.1%。

圖表呈現的是台北近幾個學年的情形。它也顯示孩子年紀越大，問題就越嚴重：在圖上的每一年，國中生的比例都遠高於國小生。這張圖無法說明數字在某一年上升或下降的原因，也不能證明戶外時間本身造成了任何改變。不過，和上述研究合起來看，它顯示保護孩子的眼睛不是一次就能完成的事，而是一種必須年復一年、在學校和家裡都持續下去的習慣。

【圖 1】台北市學生裸視視力不良率（2014–2025 學年，%）：國小從 2014 年的 49.44% 降到 2019 年的 43.51%，之後回升到 2023 年的 45.02%，2025 年為 44.35%；國中從 2014 年的 77.67% 降到 2025 年的 72.13%，每一年都比國小高。
